title: BLOCK-40: block decoding saves one logarithm at the same fractional sample index

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and shift s modulo N,n=ceil(log2N),the single BLOCK-40 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise m the least integer with m^5>=n^2,kappa=ceil(log2m)+1,base=ceil(n/(m+1)-m/2)+1,s0=kappa+1,dl=base+s0,H=base+m-1,L=floor(m/(4s0)),input widths base+i+min(s0,floor((m-1-i)s0/L)) and root1,exact binary/radix/high-part instrument,Kc=8192(m+10u+100),Kp=8192(u+100),u=ceil(log2n),capped extraction and full signed-near-parity/bootstrap/two-adic decoder) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every execution branch total charged work O(n^(17/5)2^F(n)),including gates,bit operations,lookups,addresses,source costs,initialization,resets and discarded attempts. Here F(n)=n^(3/5)+(1/2)n^(2/5)-n^(1/5). The exact growth index is3/5. All four envelopes hold jointly; logarithmic envelopes at n=1 usepositive n=2 values. Finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) are included only through outer constants; main guards apply only on the main branch. The generalized batch usesh unused top bits and exact block scoring withb0=floor(log2n),Lblk=ceil(n/b0); the entire odd and two-adic block decoder and reduced global acquisition cap are given in Sections9..13. All branch bounds remain joint.
